sections.h2: Who values and who bills property in Garrard County, KY?
sections.html:
The Garrard County PVA values every parcel, and the Garrard County Sheriff collects the tax. The PVA does not set rates or take payments, and the sheriff never assesses value, so a disagreement about the number goes to the PVA while a question about the bill goes to the sheriff.

Both offices work from 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster. The PVA is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. at (859) 792-3291, and the sheriff can be reached at (859) 792-3591. The county's site describes the PVA as a state office with local jurisdiction, supervised by the Department of Revenue, that assesses at 100 percent of fair cash value as of January 1.

The sheriff collects for 28 districts across the county, covering the state, the county, school districts and special districts such as fire protection or libraries. Bills are mailed on October 1 each year and explain due dates, penalties and what to do if a mortgage company pays. The County Clerk at 15 Public Square, Suite 5, records deeds and assists with property tax notification and collection.

sections.h2: What is Garrard County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Garrard County is in east-central Kentucky, with 230 square miles of land. Most of it is rolling Bluegrass farmland, and the southeastern corner near Cartersville falls in the Knobs region. Lancaster, the county seat and only city, began as a cluster of log cabins in 1776, and the county itself was created in 1796 from Lincoln, Mercer and Madison territory.

Daily life points toward Lexington, about 28 miles north, and Richmond and Danville are also within easy reach. Communities outside Lancaster include Paint Lick, Bryantsville, Buckeye, Cartersville, Davis Town and Hyattsville, and every resident lived in a rural area at the 2020 census. Camp Dick Robinson, the first Federal base south of the Ohio River in the Civil War, was here, and a Rural Heritage Tobacco Festival is held each September. Voters ended the county's dry status on November 7, 2023.

The numbers show a fast-growing, commuter-heavy county:

  • Estimated population in 2025: 18,207, up 7.4 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home (2020 to 2024): $204,900.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 79.9 percent, the highest of the four counties compared by the Census Bureau on this page.
  • Mean travel time to work: 33.1 minutes.
  • Building permits in 2025: 0.
  • Median gross rent: $794.

With no new permits recorded, buyers looking in Garrard County choose among existing houses, farms and acreage, which keeps older homes with deferred upkeep in play.

sections.h2: When are Garrard County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Payment is due to the sheriff by December 31, and KRS 134.015 gives a 2 percent discount if you pay everything by November 1. January adds a 5 percent penalty, and later payments add 10 percent. Because bills leave the sheriff's office on October 1, the discount period is about a month long.

If bill mailing is postponed statewide, a replacement schedule gives a month for the discount, a month at face and a month at the 5 percent charge. Taxes also remain a personal debt of the person who owned the property on the January 1 assessment date, which matters when a sale closes soon after the new year.

sections.h2: How much does a late Garrard County tax bill grow?
sections.html:
On April 15 the sheriff transfers every unpaid bill to the County Clerk, who records a lien. The Department of Revenue illustrates the cost with a $1,000 bill and an assumed 4 percent sheriff commission, so your own totals will differ.

What a $1,000 delinquent bill grows to at the clerk's office (source: Kentucky Department of Revenue)
When it is paidTotal due
At transfer from the sheriff (10 percent penalty, sheriff add-on, commission)$1,254.00
Within five business days of transfer$1,387.79
After the first county attorney notice$1,611.30
In May, with a second month of interest$1,627.61
In June, after advertising$1,659.90

Interest runs 1 percent per month. The county attorney mails a 30-day notice and a second notice, and a tax sale takes place 90 to 135 days after transfer. If a third party buys the certificate at that sale, you owe the buyer and its added fees.

sections.h2: How can a Garrard County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the PVA, then file with the County Clerk. The roll is open for 13 days from the first Monday in May, and a conference with the PVA is a precondition for an appeal. Filing must happen by close of business on the first workday after the inspection period ends.

The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after inspection and decides on documented evidence, such as comparable listings, construction costs and photographs. The board must give written reasons for any change. A person paid to represent you has to be on the state's approved list of professions and carry your written authorization.

sections.h2: What about the homestead exemption in Garrard County?
sections.html:
The exemption removes $49,100 from the assessed value of a home owned by someone 65 or older or totally disabled, for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Apply through the PVA at 319 Stanford St.

At the county's median value of $204,900, the taxable amount would be $155,800. Age is proven with a birth certificate, driver's license, passport or similar record. A seller who has held the exemption should tell the PVA after closing so it stops at that address.

faqs.q: When are Garrard County tax bills mailed?
faqs.a: They are mailed on October 1 each year, according to the Garrard County Sheriff. The 2 percent discount applies to full payment by November 1.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Garrard County tax bill looks wrong?
faqs.a: Call the Garrard County PVA at (859) 792-3291. The sheriff's office states that it never assesses value and directs value questions to the PVA.

faqs.q: Where is the Garrard County sheriff's tax office?
faqs.a: It is at 319 Stanford St. in Lancaster, KY 40444, and the number is (859) 792-3591. The sheriff collects for 28 taxing districts.

faqs.q: What happens to Garrard County taxes not paid by April 15?
faqs.a: The bill moves to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien, and interest of 1 percent per month begins, plus clerk and county attorney commissions.

faqs.q: How much is the Garrard County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. It applies to owners 65 or older or totally disabled and comes off the assessed value of the home.
